taxonomyNote: NatureServe notes American ranid genus arrangements are contested (Lithobates vs Rana); the batch name follows NatureServe's Lithobates.
fieldMarks: Well-defined round or oval dark spots with pale borders
Pale dorsolateral ridges not inset at the rear; white stripe on the upper jaw
behavior: Egg laying about April in southern Québec and the Great Lakes, later farther north
Summer use of wet meadows and fields
Eats small invertebrates at the water's edge or in fields
habitat: Near springs, slow streams, marshes, bogs, ponds and lakes with rooted aquatic vegetation; wet meadows in summer.
range: Great Slave Lake, Hudson Bay and Labrador south to southern New England, Kentucky, Nebraska, New Mexico and Arizona, west to southeastern British Columbia and eastern Washington/Oregon; spotty and partly introduced in the west.

lookalikes.name: Pickerel frog
lookalikes.howToTell: Squarish spots and yellow or orange on the hidden hind-limb and groin surfaces.

lookalikes.name: Plains leopard frog
lookalikes.howToTell: Never green, usually a pale spot on the eardrum, ridge rear ends inset.
